title: Domaine de Vieux Telegraphe: a wine dinner with this top Châteauneuf-du-Pape producer at Mauro’s Kitchen
summary: Daniel and Cecile Brunier were in town and led a wine dinner featuring their wines at the excellent Mauro’s Table,
content:
Daniel and Cecile Brunier were in town and led a wine dinner featuring their wines at the excellent Mauro’s Table, part of the Michelin-starred Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at the Owa.

Daniel was on good form, and both the food and the wine sang. The Bruniers own the famed Châteauneuf property Vieu Télégraphe, as well as Domaine les Pallières in Gigondas and a property in Ventoux. ‘It is one philosophy and one grape,’ he says, ‘Grenache, red, white and grey. Grenache makes our philosophy: we choose soil for it, we choose barrels for it and our harvesting decisions are because of the Grenache. Everything is around the Grenache.’ He says that ‘Grenache has multiple personalities depending on where it is from and who vinifies it. If you try to make a monster, you can!’

The wines are imported into the UK by Thorman Hunt, and the two have a long relationship. ‘I’m semi-retired,’ says Daniel. ‘I’m here because we’ve been friends with Jeremy Hunt and his team since the 1980s, and London is one of my favourite cities.’ He says the day to day running is now in the hands of the sixth generation, his son Edouard and his niece and nephew Manon and Nicolas. Daniel and his brother handed over to them around a decade ago. Continuity has been maintained, though. ‘Today we’ll be tasting some of the wines by the fifth generation and some by the sixth generation and it’s very difficult to see the difference.’

Daniel emphasized that the soil is much more present in the wines than winemaker technique. He also referred to the challenge posed by climate chaos. ‘We are in the south, in a hot climate, but we are not afraid of the heat: we are afraid of a lack of water,’ he says. They are allowed to irrigate if they apply for authorization, but don’t need it where they are. ‘We are in the north on a plateau, and we have a big layer of clay under the soil. It’s a sponge.’ But he adds that harvest dates have come forward more than 15 days since the early 1990s.

‘More and more we use old vines, and try to maintain them,’ says Daniel. ‘They have deep roots and can resist dry and hot summers. We also use another tool: whole bunches. We use stems more and more to reduce alcohol content and the sensation of power.’

‘Today wines are too dense and concentrated. For reds we do more infusion than extraction. We like to extract things slowly over a 30-40 day period, to keep balance and freshness.’ He adds that by making these changes they can still make wines with personality and balance as they did in the past, but he doesn’t know what will happen in the future.

Borage flowers and palourde clams
this was a superb dish. You can just see the clams; they were beautifully layered.

2023 ‘Clos Roquète’, Famille Brunier, Châteauneuf-du-Pape Blanc
This is from sandy soils (15% of the appellation has sandy soil) and it’s a blend of Clairette, which they love, Grenache Blanc and Roussanne. Textural with nice weight, showing some stoniness alongside peach and pear fruit with a liquid mineral quality and some honey and spice. Real richness allied to freshness, and quite mouthwatering. Lovely wine. 94/100

2024 ‘La Crau’, Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe, Châteauneuf-du-Pape Blanc
The vines average 60 years old and are planted on La Crau’s stony souls. Fresh and lively with nice texture and notes of pear and lemon, with a hint of apricot. Textured with some saline notes, and nice definition. 95/100

Crapaudine beetroot and caviar
This is one of the specialities of Mauro, and it’s a brilliant combination.

2020 ‘Racines’, Domaine les Pallières, Gigondas
Gigondas is a third of the size of Châteauneuf, and got its cru in 1960, 24 years later. This is 85% Grenache with Syrah and Cinsault. 90 year old vines on average. Long maceration with whole bunches. Then aged two years in large-format oak. Rich, saline and powerful with ripe cherry and berry fruits. Some blackberry and chalk, and a hint of earth in the background. Broad and expansive but still has freshness, with firm tannins and some saltiness on the finish. 94/100

Celeriac, vanilla and native lobster
There’s a sweetness to this dish that works really well.

2022 ‘Piedlong’, Famille Brunier, Châteauneuf-du-Pape
85 year old vines, mostly Grenache, 50% whole bunch. Same winemaking as Racines. This is from a flat, south-facing plateau at the highest part of the appellation (130 m). This is a newer wine made for the first time in 2011. Really elegant with fine, supple red cherries and strawberries. Quite ethereal with a sweet core to the fruit but no heaviness. Has some fine herbal notes. A beautiful expression of Grenache. 95/100

Kalibos cabbage, wildberries, Anjou pigeon
This was an amazing dish, with perfectly cooked pigeon. Stunning.

2020 ‘La Crau’, Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe, Châteauneuf-du-Pape
La Crau is the main Brunier vineyard on top of the appellation in a windy, stony location. Half of the vineyards were planted by Daniel’s grandfather, and the other half by his father. His own plantings haven’t yet made it to the Vieux Télégraphe blend. 2020 was a hot, sunny vintage. The blend is 60% Grenache, 15% Syrah, 15% Mourvèdre and then some Cinsault and Clairette. Focused and concentrated with nice intensity to the black cherry and spice, showing plenty of depth. Real presence here with sage and pepper notes, and fine-grained tannins. 95/100

2012 ‘La Crau’, Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe, Châteauneuf-du-Pape
Supple and brooding with nice black cherry and blackberry fruit, showing finesse. Supple with nice grainy detail. Beautiful fruit still, and great balance. 95/100

Cocoa mucilage, madong chocolate, almond

2025 ‘Vin du Naturel’ Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise, Domaine des Bernadins
This is not a Brunier wine, but comes from possibly the best producer in Beaumes-de-Venise. Orange peel, grapes and honey, with nice detail. This has sweet fruit but also freshness, finishing with some aniseed. 94/100

Mignardises

2011 ‘Vieux’ Marc de Vieux Télégraphe
Really impressive but I didn’t take notes.

title: Exploring the Roussillon (7) Château Nadal Hainaut
summary: Château Nadal Hainaut, an organic wine producer in the Roussillon making some nice wines. This visit was with Pauline Nadal,
content:
Château Nadal Hainaut, an organic wine producer in the Roussillon making some nice wines.

This visit was with Pauline Nadal, one of the daughters of the current owners, responsible for production. She has two sisters who don’t work in the business. Pauline trained in fine arts in London at Central St Martins, and is a ceramicist. She’s pictured above with her father.

She says that wine can be a very masculine field, but along the way she has met powerful female winemakers and she realised that this is something she can do. As a ceramicist, she worked with her hands, and as a winemaker ‘I work with my hands,’ she says. Making wine, is, to her, a certain form of art. ‘It keeps my artistic mind at peace.’ One thing she did was change all the labels, which was difficult at first, but now her parents let her do all of them.

The Hainault family bought this estate back in 1826. But by 1900 there were just two daughters involved, so they had to get married and continue the story. So one of them got married to Francois Nadal, which is the family name now.

So Pauline is sixth generation. She says that her parents worked their whole life to rebuild the estate, and they are still investing in it today. It has a beautiful chapel, because before this was a monastery, with mixed farming, before the French revolution when it was dissolved.

Half of the business focuses on hospitality, with weddings from March until November the core component. This also helps them sell their wine.

They just make estate wine from 27 hectares of vines, with 10 varieties, all farmed organically. This includes a centenarian plot of Carignan.

THE WINES

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Héméré Blanc de Noirs 2024 Côtes Catalanes
White wine from Grenache Noir, direct pressed. Light, bright, taut and quite mineral with lovely focused pear and citrus fruit, with a hint of cherry. Stony and slightly mineral on the finish. 89/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut 3 Sources Macabeu 2024 Côtes Catalanes
Beautifully packaged. This is crisp and primary with nice sweet pear drop and citrus character, showing transparency and purity. There’s nice depth of fruit, but this is all about fresh, primary pear fruit. Crisp and taut. 90/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut 3 Sources Rosé de Syrah 2024 Côtes Catalanes
Pale pink in colour this is textural and focused at the same time with high carbon dioxide adding freshness to the sweet pear and peach fruit with some cherry and citrus. Fresh and linear: this is really appealing. 91/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Aurore Aux Doigts de Rosé Grenache Gris 2024 Côtes Catalanes
2 months in French oak after stainless steel fermentation. Bright, lively and a bit spicy with some mandarin and orange peel as well as cherry and pear fruit. Brisk, lively and stony on the finish. Nice purity here with lots of primary fruit. 91/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Marie 2024 Côtes Catalanes
This is 100% Chardonnay. Fermented in American oak, one-third new, and stays there for just two months. Nice primary pear fruit here with a touch of banana, showing vivid fruit and some subtle spiciness. Nice plump fruit here, and the oak is in the background. 89/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Alexandrie Muscat Sec 2023 Côtes Catalanes
This is Muscat d’Alexandrie. Lovely aromatics here with table grapes, honey and fine spices. This is fresh and direct, a lovely dry Muscat that’s expressive and floral and bright. 91/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Grenache 2023 Côtes Catalanes
5 day maceration. Light in colour. Supple with some stewed strawberry and cherry fruit with a bit of spicy white pepper framing. Such drinkability to this wine. Supple and fun. 91/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut 3 Sources Syrah Sans Sulfites Ajoutés 2024 Côtes Catalanes
One day maceration. This is plump and rounded with nice textured cherry and strawberry fruit. Pure and supple with plummy fruit and some nice warmth, showing rounded texture. Very appealing and reassuring. 92/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut 1900 Centenaire Carignan 2023 Côtes Catalanes
Unoaked. Bright, fresh and vivid with a nice stony edge to the supple black cherry and raspberry fruit with a bit of tarry, herby character. Expressive and drinkable, with a savoury, restrained character. 91/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Odyssée 2019 Côtes du Roussillon
This is a blend, but mostly Grenache Noir, with some Syrah. This has plump cherry and berry fruit with nice drinkability, showing some strawberry richness, too. Has some spice and a touch of pepper, as well as some wild herbs. 91/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Terre de Quarante 2020 Côtes du Roussillon
Mostly Syrah and a bit of Grenache Noir (40%). One year in oak, one quarter new. Bold, juicy, some nice bright cherry and plum fruit with a bit of tarry, spicy oak in the mix. Grippy with a touch of reduction. Has a savoury twist. 89/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Hydre de Lac Sans Sulfites Ajoutés 2019 Côtes du Roussillon
Syrah (70%) and Grenache, six months in oak. Spicy, savoury and quite wild with lots of flavour. Herbs, pepper, tar and then some grippy structure. There is a spicy, herby, dry savoury finish here with tertiary flavours. Complex and intriguing. 90/100

Domaine Nadal Hainaut Signum 2020 Côtes du Roussillon
This is lovely. Mainly Syrah, vinification integrale, then basket pressed. Good concentration and freshness with some black pepper and black cherry, as well as some spicy detail. Powerful but fresh with nice brightness, showing a little bit of savoury evolution. Some pepper, thyme and iodine here. Lovely detail. This is really good. 1800 bottles made. 94/100

title: Vinho Verde: Quinta da Pegadinha
summary: This is a small family vineyard and farm 15 km from the ocean, in the southern part of Vinho Verde,
content:
This is a small family vineyard and farm 15 km from the ocean, in the southern part of Vinho Verde, on the Cavado river. There are 6 hectares of vineyards, and 6 hectares given to cows and sheep. They make some cheese as well as wine.

I tasted with winemaker Felipe Lemos. The farming is integrated production, and they aren’t organic because this is too difficult with cows, says Felipe. This is because to produce the maize to feed them, it’s really difficult to avoid using some products that aren’t organic. In the vineyard the work is done with hand, and no herbicides are used.

Peghadinha Reserva Branco 2022 Vinho Verde, Portugal
Louriero. The grapes are harvested in the morning in small crates. Whole bunch pressed to 0.24 bar, then natural settling in stainless steel. Fermented in stainless steel and used French oak (half/half) with lots of lees work. Supple, fine and linear with detailed lemony fruit and some subtle saline characters. Such a lovely tension in the mouth, finishing fresh. Great balance. 94/100

Peghadinha Alvarinho Reserva 2023 Vinho Verde, Portugal
This is the second harvest from four-year-old vines. 1 m 60 fruiting wire, with umbrella sprawl of canopy to protect grapes from the sun. There’s a fabric mulch in the vine row. Pressed to 0.6 bar then fermented and aged in stainless steel. Fresh and aromatic with apricot and lemon notes, as well as lovely texture in the mouth. Bright and fruity with slight salinity. Fine spicy detail, showing expressive fruit. There’s a crystalline quality to this wine. 93/100

Peghadinha Padeiro Grande Escolha 2023 Vinho Verde, Portugal
This is foot-trodden in stainless steel tanks and given a cold maceration of 48 hours. Then it is fermented off the skins. Full pink/red in colour, this is bright and juicy, and so fragrant with lovely redcurrant fruit as well as nice acidity and a bit of crunch. Pretty and expressive with good intensity. Bright, linear and delicious. 92/100

title: Criante, a natural wine producer from Sicily
summary: Website: https://www.criante.it/ Criante is a natural wine producer based in Alcamo, western Sicily. The Adragane family have a mixed farm,
content:
Website: https://www.criante.it/

Criante is a natural wine producer based in Alcamo, western Sicily. The Adragane family have a mixed farm, with 15 hectares of vines over two locations, and about the same area producing other agricultural products. The farm has been in the family a long time, but it’s only since 2019 that the project has been called Criante. Although there is a DOC for Alcamo, they don’t use it because the appellation rules require interventions that they aren’t going to do in the winemaking process.

Criante Catarratto Frizzante Niente Panico Pet Nat 2024 Sicily, Italy
Lovely balance here. Very fresh and focused with crisp citrus and white peach. Nice balance with some yeasty richness. 92/100

Criante C24 2024 Sicily, Italy
This is Catarratto from Contrada Valle. Lovely intensity and personality with pear, peach and some almond. Such amazing texture, and so expressive. 94/100

Criante G24 2024 Sicily, Italy
This is Grillo from Contrada Modica, which is a vineyard close to the sea. Open, textural and fine with lovely pear and lemon fruit with some chalkiness. Fresh but with texture. Open and expressive with nice balance. 93/100

Criante C21 M 2021 Sicily, Italy
This is Catarratto from Contrada Valle macerated on skins for 8 days. Pear, peach and some mint, with a nice bitter twist to the palate, and some almond character. Textural and expressive. 92/100

Criante P22 2022 Sicily, Italy
This is Perricone from Contrada Valle. Sweetly aromatic with a savoury edge to the ripe barriers and cherry, with a bit of grip. Slightly oxidative in style, but showing nice balance. 92/100

Criante N22 2022 Sicily, Italy
This is Nero d’Avola from Contrada Valle, 10% aged in large barrels for 6 months. There’s a nice savoury, bitter edge to the bright cherry and berry fruits with a grippy finish and some sour cherry at the end. 92/100

Criante Rossocriante 2020 Sicily, Italy
50% Perricone and 50% Nero d’Avola. Aged in new barriques. Slightly baked nose is savoury and spicy with some earthy hints. The palate is ripe, spicy and evolved. 90/100

UK agent: Sager and Wine

title: Celebrating 25 years of Filipa Pato’s wines with an amazing lunch and tasting
summary: Flipa Pato, daughter of famous Bairrada winegrower Luis Pato, first started making her own wines 25 years ago, in 2001.
content:
Flipa Pato, daughter of famous Bairrada winegrower Luis Pato, first started making her own wines 25 years ago, in 2001. She was aged 25, and the wines stood out as really impressive from the outset.

Gradually she added to these holdings. And Belgian restaurateur and sommelier William Wouters was another acquisition (he joined the project in 2006 and they married in 2008), and now the wines are labelled Filipa Pato and William Wouters. He’s brought another dimension to the project, but it’s Filipa who does the winemaking.

Bairrada is an amazing wine region, but it hasn’t always been well respected. This is now changing, and Filipa’s father Luis deserves quite a bit of credit for this. Initially he was quite a modernist, but he always kept his love for Baga, the principal red grape of the region.

For a while Luis left the appellation, but then he came back. Seen as a modernist, he ruffled feathers. But the modernists who caused the real trouble were those who replanted vineyards with international (French) varieties. They aren’t needed here.

Bairrada has amazing old vineyards, and not just red (Baga), but also white. The key to the success of this region is largely down to the soils, and partly due to the climate. Much of the region is limestone, with some clay in the mix. But as with other fine wine regions, there’s diversity in the terroir. Consider Bairrada as similar to Burgundy or Barolo, where site-specific differences can be realized in the wines.

There’s now a critical mass of producers making excellent wines in the region, with a clear focus on Baga as the key red variety. As well as Filipa and Wouter’s wines, we have Vadio, Quinta de Baixo (Niepoort), Gonçalves Faria and newcomer Transmission. And then there’s Luis Pato, Quinta das Bágeiras, Sidónio de Sousa, Quinta da Vacariça and Caves São João.

In the winery, Filipa’s approach to élevage encompasses a range of tanks and vessels, including quite a lot of clay. She even has a basket press that she designed herself. For Baga, she uses 30-40% whole bunch, not 100%. ‘I like a bit,’ she says. ‘It gives more drinkability, and I appreciate the vibrancy.’ She puts the whole clusters at the bottom of the tank, crushes it with feet, then puts destemmed grapes on top, and then on top of this more whole cluster. She might use more or less whole cluster depending on how full the tanks are: she ferments each plot separately, and doesn’t like to have half-full tanks. So if the tank is looking like it might not be full, she’ll put more whole cluster in because this takes more room.

The winery, near their home in Óis de Bairro. Is relatively new. It’s much more practical than the old one. And next to it there’s a new wine bar, Nossa, offering Filipa and William’s wines, but also a nice selection of grower Champagnes that they import.

Before the celebrations, I visited some of the oldest plots that she has. Filipa began with three rented plots in 2001, and started buying vineyards in 2006.

Over the last few years she has been busy buying old vineyards and then renovating them. Currently Filipa and William have 20 hectares split over 37 plots.

The first plot we look at is one of the centenarian plots that goes into Nossa, and this is where the pigs are.

The second is an old vineyard called Careca: the grapes from this are fermented separately, and at some stage this will be a future cuvée in its own right. Then the third is the oldest, the Missão vineyard, which according to official records was planted in 1864. This is before phylloxera and the vines are ungrafted. It’s a remarkable plot, with wizened old vines. The trunks aren’t as thick as you might think, and this is presumably because of the bony soils. There’s a soil pit, showing a thin layer of clay topsoil over almost pure limestone. The plot is also east facing, which is ideal.

PIGS

Key to farming the old vineyards is the use of pigs. You can spot Filipa’s plots because they are all securely fenced, and each has a small structure where the pigs can get shade and cover.

Filipa introduced animals because she wanted to help regenerate the soils. She farms biodynamically, and when she took over conventionally farmed vineyards it was taking up to a decade to recover the soils to full life. So she introduced animals to help with this process.

First she began with sheep, the animal of choice for many vineyards. But far too often the sheep were being attacked by hunters’ dogs. ‘In 2020, during Covid, we thought why not put the pigs on the vineyard?’ says Filipa. After all, Bairrada is famous for pigs: it is the home of Leitão, the suckling pig that’s the staple dish in restaurants of the region.  

Filipa is using smaller pigs that are a cross between Vietnamese pigs and bizarro and Serrano, the two local pigs for Leitão. They work well, and because they are crosses they are hardy enough to live outside all year. And they aren’t troubled by dogs.

These pigs are moved from one parcel to another, and although they can’t be used all year round, they are focused on the ground and you get two months’ longer vineyard residence time than you do with sheep. The fences need to be good. ‘We can’t have male and female together,’ says Filipa. ‘If the ladies don’t give the men attention when they are suckling the males go away to the village.’ Escaping pigs have been the cause of many phone calls and call outs. Currently Filipa has 9 pigs, but two of the females are pregnant.

DRONES

Another innovation has been the use of drone spraying, which she does from the beginning of May to end of June when there is a big mildew pressure. The advantage of the drone is that there’s no compaction of the soil (for vineyards where tractors would be used) and it’s much less work than back-pack spraying, which is how they treat the old vineyards (you can’t get tractors into them). ‘Since we have the drone we can spray every week,’ says Filipa, whereas before they could only really spray every fortnight. ‘It’s like a PlayStation,’ she says. ‘The young guys do it.’

Here’s the catch, though. In the EU, drone use for spraying  agrochemicals isn’t allowed. The fear is spray drift. And this includes the biodynamic/organic fungicides elemental sulfur and copper-based products.

Filipa uses it to spray plant-derived products, such as teas derived from horsetail and willow, and some essential oils. And these have proven quite effective. This year for plant protection (2026) she used no copper at all in the vineyards (this would have to be back pack sprayed), but this was the first time.

The drone has also been really helpful with the olive trees. It does 3 m high passes and so it sprays them as well, and as a result they’ve had higher yields of olives and are now able to commercialise the oil.

There’s another use for the drone: it can be used to seed cover crops. The idea here is that when you want to sow a cover crop it can often be a bad time to access the vineyard. Filipa has a device that attaches to the drone which then spreads her se.ed mix throughout the vineyard

The drone she has is made by DJI, who are the world’s leading drone-producing company. They also make amazing gimbals and film camera all-in-one rigs. It’s one of the smaller agricultural drones (or UAVs, for uncrewed aerial vehicle, the official term) with a capacity for 22 litres. She bought it for treating the unmechanizable old vineyards, but she also uses it for the first two treatments of the mechanizable vineyards.

THE LUNCH, BY SÁLA

This lunch, celebrating 25 years of Filipa Pato, was quite remarkable. It was cooked by the team from Sála in Lisbon, the restaurant of João Sa. Everything was spot on, and some of the dishes were truly exciting.

  • Buffalo Pato Tart
  • Puri with prawn tatare
  • Aged amberjack, green curry and baobab
  • Traditional couscous from Trás-os-Montes, striped prawn and tom yum
  • Monkfish and mushrooms
  • Bairrada style moray eel
  • Lupin beans, fig and beer
  • Truffles and chocolate
  • Almond and white miso

WINES

Filipa Pato & William Wouters 3B Blanc de Blancs NV Bairrada, Portugal
A blend of Bical (70%), Maria Gomes (23%) and Cercial (7%). Fresh and linear with nice vivid citrus and pear fruit some crisp green apple, and lovely chalky, salty mineral notes.  Quite delicious. 91/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Vinha Maria Rinchoa Brut Nature 2021 Bairrada, Portugal
This is from a single plot, and the base wine is a blend of Baga, Bical, Cercial, Arinto, Maria Gomes and Rabo de Ovelha, wild ferment in cask with so sulfites. Tirage under cork, disgorged three months ago. Full gold in colour this is powerful and lively with bold citrus fruit and a bit of toast. Complex and layered with some salinity and real focus, showing vivid citrus fruit. Not as rich as the colour would suggest. 94/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Nossa Calcário Bical Branco 2025 Bairrada, Portugal (magnum)
Lively, with lovely acidity. Stony and bright with a nice mineral character under the lemon and lime fruit. So crystalline and linear; stony and refined. 95/100

Filipa Pato & William Nossa T.la Bical 2022 Wouters Bairrada, Portugal
11% alcohol. Tola means crazy in Portuguese. This was the first vineyard that Filipa and William bought together and this cuvée spends longer (18 months) on the lees than the regular Bical. Massive concentration here with taut, mineral lemon and lime fruit as well as some waxiness. This has real density, and it is still quite primary. Beautiful saline streak running through it. 96/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Nossa Calcário Baga Vinhas Velhas 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (magnum)
Supple with some meatiness and a bit of spicy wildness. It’s fresh, with a savoury twisyt to the vivid black cherry and plum fruit. 93/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Nossa Calcário Baga Vinhas Velhas 2015 Bairrada, Portugal (magnum)
At 11 years old this is linear and concentrated showing nice acidity and some good tannic structure. It’s still fresh, but it is showing some development. Chalky and linear with a slight tarry note. Fresh with some maturity. 95/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Missão 2023 Bairrada, Portugal (magnum)
Focused, fresh and mineral this shows lovely black cherry fruit with some spice and pepper, as well as rosemary and redcurrant. Lovely texture and focus. Multidimensional with amazing acid line and refinement. 97/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Missão 2015 Bairrada, Portugal (magnum)
Savoury, spicy and firm, showing lovely structure and nice acidity. Quite mineral, showing freshness and elegance. Really refined, and grainy and nourishing with it. 95/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Flos Castanea 2023 Bairrada, Portugal
This is really interesting because it’s a collaboration with a biodynamic Vinho Verde producer who uses chestnut flower instead of sulfites as a preservative. It’s Bical, fermented on skins, and then half is aged in cask and half in amphora. Saline and spicy with ripe apple and citrus, showing some tanginess and a lovely acid line. So distinctive and quite beautiful with real detail. 96/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters Espirito Baga 2020 Bairrada, Portugal
This is fortified Baga. Before Filipa made it she phoned Dirk Niepoort for advice. She was under the impression that she should harvest late for fortified, but he said harvest at the same time as Nossa. This is whole cluster foot-trodden for 3-4 days, then fermentation is stopped. A bit of spirit is added at this stage, then the wine is pressed and fortified up to 19.5% alcohol before ageing in cask. Dirk said to her that one of the secrets is that to make great vintage-style Port you have to use very old casks (high alcohol is too extractive for younger casks) and he sent some old casks from Gaia. This has 90 g/l of sugar, and spent 3 years in Port pipes. Fresh, spicy, vital, tannic and firm. Still very youthful and quite delicious, with brooding dark fruits. 94/100

Filipa Pato & William Wouters S.l.ra NV Bairrada, Portugal
This is a traditional method sparkling wine made from a base wine blend that contains all the vintages since 2001 (for S.l.ra read ‘solera’). Three years on the lees. Powerful with lime, toast, spice and honey on the nose. Tangy and energetic with good acidity and a touch of sour cherry. Lovely energy to this expressive wine. 93/100

title: Video: with Filipa Pato in her old vineyards in Bairrada, Portugal, which she farms with the help of pigs
summary: Filipa Pato began making her own wines in 2001, starting with three rented plots. Since then she and her husband
content: Filipa Pato began making her own wines in 2001, starting with three rented plots. Since then she and her husband William Wouter have been acquiring vineyards, some of them more than 100 years old. These are mostly planted with the red grape Baga, and she now has 20 hectares spread over 37 different plots, which are farmed biodynamically. I spent some time visiting a few of these amazing vineyards with her and one of her US importers Steve Meier. She has been using pigs to regenerate the vineyards with great success.

title: Highlights: Overgaauw Sylvaner 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
summary: This wine is noteworthy because it is South Africa’s only Sylvaner, first made in 1971. Just a single hectare of
content:
This wine is noteworthy because it is South Africa’s only Sylvaner, first made in 1971. Just a single hectare of this variety in the ground (first planted in the 1960s). It has a reputation for ageing well, and I can believe that.

Overgaauw Sylvaner 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is really interesting with a smoky edge to the sweet apple, yellow plum and peach fruit. Quite pure and nicely textured with some volume on the palate, finishing with a spicy flourish and bold melon and pear fruit. I really like the distinctive smoky spiciness here. Bold, and very stylish. 93/100 (£19.98 Museum Wines)

title: Rabasco: beautiful natural wines from Abruzzo, Italy
summary: Website: https://www.rabascowinery.com/en/home-en-2/ Rabasco is an impressive natural wine producer in Abruzzo, which is run by Iole Rabasco. She was previously
content:
Website: https://www.rabascowinery.com/en/home-en-2/

Rabasco is an impressive natural wine producer in Abruzzo, which is run by Iole Rabasco. She was previously a lawyer, but decided to take over the family winery in the 2000s, farming the 11 hectare estate organically (later switching to biodynamics in 2006) and making the wines naturally. The estate, with four separate vineyards, is based in the village of Pianella, in Pescara, and the vineyards have age (over 40 years old). The big advantage from her point is that they’ve never been conventionally farmed. These are zero/zero wines with no added sulfites.

One feature here is the use of demijohns for some of the wines (indicated by Damigiana in the name). Iole has 120 of them! The labels – hand drawn – are beautifully retro and fit the wines well. I tasted these wines at the VinNatur tasting in Paris, November 2025.

Rabasco Cancelli Branco 2024 Abruzzo, Italy
10% alcohol. This is Trebbiano d’Abruzzo, harvested at the end of August and direct pressed into stainless steel. Full yellow in colour, this is bright and lively, and even has some structure, with really fine acidity. Lemony, showing good concentration, this is pithy and has lots of personality. 93/100

Rabasco La Salita 2024 Abruzzo, Italy
11.5% alcohol. This is made from an old clone of Trebbiano d’Abruzzo, fermented and aged in stainless steel. There’s great concentration here, showing lemon, orange peel, pear and apple. Nice depth and richness, with a grainy, detailed palate, and finishing with some fine spicy notes, and apple, cherry and dried herb characters. 94/100

Rabasco Damigiana 2024 Abruzzo, Italy
12% alcohol. This is Trebbiano d’Abruzzo with 30% Malvasia Candida, and it spends 5 days on skins. Aged in demijohns.  It’s a slightly cloudy golden colour. Textured and detailed with nice weight, showing apples, pears, some peach and and even a touch of mint. There’s some structure, there are some oxidative hints, but also real detail and finesse. Very fine. 94/100

Rabasco Cancelli Rosso 2024 Abruzzo, Italy
12.5% alcohol. This is Montepulciano d’Abruzzo, and it spends just 1.5 days on skins, and is raised in stainless steel. Supple and juicy with nice sour cherry fruit. Has some grip, and also lovely acidity. Fresh red cherry and redcurrant fruit with vibrancy. Juicy and delicious. 93/100

Rabasco Damigiana Rosato 2024 Abruzzo, Italy
This is from a young vineyard of Cerusualo. Full pink/orange in colour, and this is just from the press! Lively, with tangy redcurrant fruit as well as red cherry, with citrus brightness. There are some grippy tannins here, and good acidity. So interesting. 93/100

Rabasco Rosso Damigiana 2020 IGT Colline Pescaresi, Abruzzo, Italy
Montepulciano d’Abruzzo with 9 days on skins, then raised in demijohns. Beautiful texture here to the bright red cherry and raspberry fruit. Grippy and firm with good acidity and some sleekness to the red fruit. Substantial, fine and expansive, with lots of tannin. 94/100

title: With these twelve wines, Juampi Michellini, Matias Riccitelli, Rafael Urreloja and Derek Mossman Knapp illustrate Argentina and Chile’s precocious ability to express the best in any variety
summary: Twelve wines, selected by their maker, four from Zorzal and four from Riccitelli, Undurraga and The Garage Wines Company, were
content:
Twelve wines, selected by their maker, four from Zorzal and four from Riccitelli, Undurraga and The Garage Wines Company, were poured

Of twelve wines tasted, only one was Malbec

Jamie Goode and Lisse Garnett report

Matias Riccitelli

Riccitelli wines command near cultish respect from the initiated, allocations always sell out, and yet the man is genuine, softly spoken and modest. He clearly has a great passion for the wines he is making from Patagonia, as well as in Las Compuertas and Monasterio in Mendoza.

Bastardo, Old Vines From Patagonia 2024

Alcohol 12%, 100% Bastardo aka Trousseau. Grapes sourced from a vineyard in Patagonia, planted in the 70s by some unknown lost lover of this Jura variety. We too love this grape for its dark colour, spice and dried floral notes – the lightness and power it seems to convey and its ultimate silky passage down my gullet. 

Lighter coloured, this is whole bunch fermented, after being foot crushed to avoid carbonic maceration, and then pressed to foudres. Supple and fresg with iron, blood, red cherries, plums and spice. Focused with nice precision: so expressive. 94/100

Semillon, Old Vines From Patagonia 2024 

Alcohol 12%,100% Semillon. An insanely complex, gorgeous wine that will only get better – its honeyed and waxy and fragrant with jasmine, hay, vanilla and candied lemon. Just so pretty, nutty and layered – we were having so much fun that I was unable to contemplate this wine as it deserves, a bottle is an event – I don’t think he makes much and I want more.

Old vines, picked early. Crystalline and light with focused citrus fruit. There’s a bright salinity from some flor aging of some of the wine. Beautiful, expressive, saline and complex. 95/100 (JG)

Pinot Noir, La Carrera 2024 Uco Valley
This is from a new 1700 m site, with some calcareous content in the soils. 30% whole bunch then foudres for 12 months. Ripe but fresh, supple with bright cherry and plum fruit. Very fine and expressive, and juicy and focused. Such presence here. 94/100 (JG)

Chardonnay La Carrera 2024 Uco Valley
From calcareous soils and fermented in foudre. Mineral, fine, fresh and expressive with lovely spiciness. Textural and linear. 95/100 (JG)

Rafael Urrejola, Head Winemaker Undurraga

Modesty again from this highly accomplished winemaker with a voice fit for broadcasting. His family emigrated from the Basque region, from near Gijon, three hundred years ago. They were always connected to wine, but he is the first to turn professional. Cool climate wines became his speciality by default early on in Leyda. He joined what was then a traditional Undurraga in 2007 to initiate Terroir Hunter, a series of radically innovative terroir-specific wines made from carefully chosen and extremely diverse regions. Terroir Hunter has made many experimental wines, driving the need for a sense of place in Chilean viticulture. Urrejola is a champion of Chilean diversity, and he believes multitudinous terroirs, ocean influence and altitude make anything possible in this long, slim country.

Undurraga Terroir Hunter Pinot Noir, Trama 2022

13.5% Alcohol. From a block on limestone in San Antonio Valley, rare in Chile. The climate here is cool and is only five kilometres from the Ocean. Refined, subtle, elegant and fresh, with 25% on stems, gently extracted, indigenous yeast and aged in concrete. Beautifully alive with strawberry, cherry and a fragrant waft of dried aromatic herbs and white pepper. Juicy, sapid and delicious.

Supple and bright with nice concentration, showing sweet raspberry and cherry fruit. Nice compact fruit here with good depth and some crunchy tannins, finishing bright. 94/100 (JG)

Undurraga Terroir Hunter Chardonnay 2023 Limari Valley
13% alcohol. This is a bright, expressive Chardonnay offering orange peel and mandarin notes as well as pear, apricot and spice. But there’s also lovely acidity offsetting this ripe fruit. Lovely. 94/100 (JG)

Undurraga Carmenere Extinto 2022 Cachapoal Valley
14% alcohol. Bright blackcurrant fruit with vibrancy, and some black cherry notes. Focused and rich with some nice spiciness. Intense, salty and mineral. 94/100 (JG)

Undurraga Garnacha Cauquenes 2021 Maule Valley
14.5% alcohol. Garnacha was grafted onto old vines in Cauquenes. Black cherry and blackberry fruit, showing juiciness and a sense of harmony. Lovely. 92/100 (JG)

Juampi Michelini

I was once told Michelini’s are like mushrooms, they spring up everywhere in the wine world – it can be confusing. Juampi aka Juan Pablo Michelini created Zorzal with his brothers Heraldo? And Matias, to create wines that are not market driven but reflect the calcareous mountain terroir from which they came. The Michelini’s have been making groundbreaking wines with little oak and almost no intervention for decades. They drove the vanguard of change in Argentina, harvesting early and looking for cool expression. 

Juampi, “Argentina used to be another country in terms of wine but the 90s style of bold Malbec, hot wine – over oaked, over matured, we didn’t know anything about soils then but we had some certainty about altitude, we knew we wanted freshness, finesse and elegance.” 

Argentina has moved toward terroir specific wines collectively, but the Michelini’s played a star role in that movement.

Zorzal Malbec, Gran Terroir 2024 Uco Valley
13.5% Alcohol, grown on four parcels of limestone and sand, destemmed and fermented in concrete vats its dry – it has texture, tension, Juampi says they have too much, flavour and texture in the grapes so they pair back through low intervention, and ‘infuse’ the grapes. The wine spends one year in old 500 litre barrels.

Ripe but balanced. Fresh and supple with black cherries, plums and spice. Nice black cherry and blackberry fruit here with a grippy edge. This is really good. 94/100 (JG)

Zorzal Chardonnay Terroir Unico 2024 Uco Valley
12.5% alcohol. Lively and powerful with lively citrus and pear fruit as well as some chalky detail. Lovely freshness with good acidity. Fine and crystalline. 93/100 (JG)

Zorzal Eggo Franco Cabernet Franc 2024 Uco Valley
14.5% alcohol. Matured in concrete eggs. Complex, ripe and rich with lovely blackberry fruit. Rich, full and dense with bold ripe fruit and some grainy tannins. Salty, mineral finish. 94/100 (JG)

Zorzal Chardonnay Parcelario 2024 Uco Valley
This is the ‘grand cru’ level. It’s a block of Chardonnay with sme limestone under the soil. Fresh, bright and linear with nice weight and complexity. Such a beautiful wine. 95/100 (JG)

Derek Mossman Knapp, Garage Wines

Derek Knapp has been leading the Maule charge for a long time, and making some excellent wine under the Garage Wines label. Dry farming, old vines, good farming. And cool labelling, too.

Garage Wines Garnacha Carinena Monastrell Parcel Series Sauzal Vineyard Empedrado The Ploughmen 2019 Maule
14.5% alcohol. There’s a savoury, spicy edge to the nose with ripe blackberry and black cherry fruit, as well as some earthy hints. Grippy, fresh and focused with juicy fruit and a bit of tannin, finishing firm and structured. 91/100 (JG)

Garage Wines Single Ferment Old Vine Pale Rosado 2023 Maule
Pale pink in colour. Fresh, supple and bright with nice acidity and juicy cherry and raspberry fruit, with just a bit of grip. Fine, sappy and delicious. 91/100 (JG)

Garage Wines Cabernet Sauvignon Parcel Selection Renacido Vineyard 2021 Maule
Firm but supple at the same time with bright black cherry and blackberry fruit. Juicy with nice focus and some structure, as well as good acidity. No new oak here, and it works very well. 94/100 (JG)

Garage Wines Truquilemu Syrah Lot 84 2019 Maule
Bold, taut and structured with nice black cherry fruit. Grippy, dense and linear with cherries and plums, and some reductive detail. 92/100 (JG)

title: Three wines from a new producer in Oxfordshire (UK): Yew Tree Vineyard
summary: Website: https://yewtreevineyard.com/ Yew Tree is a 5 hectare vineyard in South Oxfordshire, with vines planted in 2015 and 2020 on
content:
Website: https://yewtreevineyard.com/

Yew Tree is a 5 hectare vineyard in South Oxfordshire, with vines planted in 2015 and 2020 on greensand soils. After selling all the grapes for several years (I’ve tried wines from Black Book and Gutter & Stars from their fruit), they now have their own wines, with 2025 the first vintage. They are made and bottled at contract winery Defined Wines. These are priced at £19 direct to consumer.

Yew Tree Ortega 2025 Oxfordshire, England
12.5% alcohol. This is bright, juicy and fruity with a slight grapey edge to the citrus fruit. Juicy and tasty with direct fruit the main theme. It’s very clean with real ripeness as well as good acidity. 88/100

Yew Tree Bacchus 2025 Oxfordshire, England
11.5% alcohol. This is bright and energetic with nice crisp elderflower and citrus fruit, as well as a hint of table grape. Pure and focused with nice concentration, and bracing acidity on the finish. A lovely expression of Bacchus in a dry, tight style, but with plenty of varietal character. 90/100

Yew Tree Rosé 2025 Oxfordshire, England
12% alcohol. This is a blend of Pinot Noir and Pinot Precoce. Appealing mid-pink in colour, this is juicy and fruity with some vibrant raspberry and redcurrant, as well as strawberries and cream. There’s a nice energy to this wine, and it’s very fruit forward and appealing. 89/100
